checks.details: pure gas and pure ice stay put above and below saturation (3 draws)
supersaturation deposits ice and undersaturation sublimates it (3 draws)
at saturation phi_t = -M dF/dphi with M > 0, so F decreases (3 draws, phi = 0.3 and 0.7)

relaxation: M*(-6*eps*gamma*(Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (x, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (y, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (z, 2))) + 6*gamma*(1 - 2*phi(x, y, z, t))*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*phi(x, y, z, t)/eps)
driving force: -30*alpha*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))**2*(rho_v(x, y, z, t) - rho_vs(T(x, y, z, t)))*phi(x, y, z, t)**2

relaxation: - 3*M*eps*(Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (x, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (y, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (z, 2))) + 3*M/eps*phi(x, y, z, t)*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*(1 - 2*phi(x, y, z, t))
driving force: -alpha/rho_i*phi(x, y, z, t)**2*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))**2*(rho_v(x, y, z, t) - rho_vs(T(x, y, z, t)))

agent's symbols.name: M
agent's symbols.meaning: interface mobility (Allen-Cahn kinetic coefficient): how fast $\phi$ relaxes down the gradient of $F$; with it a curved interface moves at $v_n=-6\gamma\varepsilon M\kappa$

agent's symbols.name: alpha
agent's symbols.meaning: deposition/sublimation rate coefficient; a flat interface advances into the gas at $v_n = 6\varepsilon\alpha(\rho_v-\rho_{vs})$, so $6\varepsilon\alpha = k/\rho_i$ with $k$ a kinetic mass-transfer velocity (Hertz-Knudsen: $k=a_s\sqrt{k_BT/2\pi m}$) and $\rho_i$ the ice density

agent's symbols.name: p(phi)
agent's symbols.meaning: interface-localizing function $30\phi^2(1-\phi)^2$, zero in bulk ice and gas, $\int_0^1 p\,d\phi = 1$

agent's symbols.name: phi_0(n)
agent's symbols.meaning: equilibrium flat-interface profile along the normal coordinate $n$

agent's symbols.name: n
agent's symbols.meaning: coordinate normal to a flat interface, pointing into the ice

agent's symbols.name: v_n
agent's symbols.meaning: normal velocity of the interface, positive when ice grows

agent's symbols.name: kappa
agent's symbols.meaning: sum of principal curvatures of the interface (positive for a convex ice grain)

agent left out.effect: Anisotropy of ice surface energy and kinetics (faceting)
agent left out.why: Taken as isotropic: $\gamma$, $M$ and $\alpha$ are scalars. This is acceptable for rounded pore-scale grains; anisotropy would add orientation-dependent factors.
Kept constant for simplicity. Their Arrhenius or $\sqrt{T}$ variation can be restored by writing $M(T)$ and $\alpha(T)$ without changing the form of the equation.
The pore vapor is close to saturation ($|\rho_v-\rho_{vs}|/\rho_{vs}\ll1$), so the linear term is the leading order and the dropped terms are $O((\Delta/\rho_{vs})^2)$.

agent left out.effect: Curvature dependence of the saturation density (explicit Gibbs-Thomson term in $\rho_{vs}$)
agent left out.why: It is represented by the $M$-term ($v_n\propto-\kappa$). Matching $6\gamma\varepsilon M=6\varepsilon\alpha\rho_{vs}\gamma/(\rho_i R_vT)\cdot$(molar factors) would make it quantitative; that choice is left to the calibration of $M$. The size is $\rho_{vs}\gamma/(\rho_iR_vT\,r)\sim10^{-4}\rho_{vs}$ for $r\sim1\,\mu$m.

agent left out.effect: Mechanical stress, elasticity and grain motion of ice and regolith
agent left out.why: The regolith grains and ice are treated as rigid; stresses are outside this model.
Deterministic model; noise is needed only for nucleation, which is excluded.

agent left out.effect: Wetting of regolith grains by ice (contact angle at grain walls)
agent left out.why: Boundary conditions at the grain surfaces are taken as natural (no-flux), as needed to drop the boundary term in S1; a wetting energy would add a surface term.
